correctness.rationale: The open-neighbor count at a_i is |B|-1_{i in B}; for even n=2k the three possibilities (zero, complement of balanced opposite shore, one) imply every image periodic, exactly c+2 fixed states, (c+2)^2 periodic states, and (c+2)(c+1)/2 primitive period-two orbits with F^3=F. For odd n=2k+1 the four exact tie branches lead to the stated fixed-state decomposition. The bundled exact rational Fourier–Motzkin source treats the four paired atom types, checks branch feasibility for five steps, and uses a 608-cell nonfixed F^2=I search with two feasible uniform extreme branches; the verifier is finite-dimensional but universally parametrized, not merely a small-n numerical extrapolation. An independent literal-neighbor enumeration verified n=3..7: (fixed,two-orbits,max entry)=(20,1,2),(8,28,1),(82,1,3),(22,231,1),(352,1,3). The stronger earlier analytic six-case proof independently supports the same all-size formulas.
residual_risks: The rational feasibility checker treats a superset of integer atom counts; it is sound for ruling out disallowed cells but would not prove integer feasibility by itself. Existence is supplied by explicit odd opposing uniform states and constructive sharp-depth examples. Replaying all code is not a substitute for verifying elimination logic.
